content: Certainly. 1. Rama Rao S, Lacuest M, Costello M, Pangolibay B, Jones H conducted a study exploring the relationship between the quality of healthcare services and the utilization of contraceptives. This was published in the International Family Planning Perspectives in 2003, volume 29, issue 2, pages 76–83. 2. Sanogo D, Rama Rao S, Johnes H, N’diaye PM’bow B, and Diop CB investigated strategies to enhance the quality of care and the use of contraceptives in Senegal. Their findings were published in the African Journal of Reproductive Health in 2003, volume 7, pages 57–73. 3. The World Health Organization (WHO) released the second edition of Safe Abortion: Technical and Policy Guidance for Health Systems in 2012, providing comprehensive guidelines for safe abortion practices. 4. Guyatt GH, Oxman AD, Vist GE, Kunz R, Falck-Ytter Y, Alonso-Coello P, et al. introduced the GRADE system, which represents a consensus framework for rating the quality of evidence and the strength of recommendations. This was detailed in the BMJ in 2008, volume 336, issue 7650, pages 924–926. 5. Schunemann HJ, Oxman AD, Brozek J, Glasziou P, Bossuyt P, Chang S, et al. applied the GRADE system to assess the quality of evidence for diagnostic recommendations. This was published in Evidence-Based Medicine in 2008, volume 13, issue 6, pages 162–163. 6. Jaeschke R, Guyatt GH, Dellinger P, Schunemann H, Levy MM, Kunz R, et al. discussed the use of the GRADE grid to facilitate decision-making in clinical practice guidelines when consensus is difficult to achieve. This was published in the BMJ in 2008, volume 337, article a744. 7. Barbui C, Dua T, van Ommeren M, Yasamy MT, Fleischmann A, Clark N, et al. highlighted the challenges in developing evidence-based recommendations using the GRADE approach, particularly in the context of mental, neurological, and substance use disorders. This was published in PLoS Medicine in 2010, volume 7, issue 8, article e1000322. 8. The Committee on Economic, Social, and Cultural Rights (CESCR) issued General Comment No. 20 during its 42nd session, emphasizing non-discrimination in economic, social, and cultural rights as outlined in Article 2, paragraph 2, of the International Covenant on Economic, Social, and Cultural Rights. 9. Paul Hunt, the Special Rapporteur on the Right to Health, presented a report to the Commission on Human Rights during its 60th session, focusing on the right of everyone to enjoy the highest attainable standard of physical and mental health. 10. The United Nations adopted the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women (CEDAW) in 1979, emphasizing the protection of women's rights, including equality in marriage and family relations. 11. The Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities was adopted by the United Nations General Assembly in 2006, aiming to protect the rights and dignity of individuals with disabilities. 12. The International Covenant on Economic, Social, and Cultural Rights (ICESCR), adopted in 1966, outlines the obligations of states to uphold these rights, including the right to health. 13. The United Nations Committee on the Rights of the Child issued General Comment No. 3 during its 32nd session, addressing the rights of children in the context of HIV/AIDS. 14. The WHO published the 17th Model List of Essential Medicines, which serves as a guideline for the selection of essential medicines worldwide. 15. The WHO released a fact sheet on emergency contraception, providing evidence-based information on its use and accessibility. 16. The United Nations Commission on Population and Development adopted Resolution 2012/1, focusing on adolescents and youth, during its 45th session. 17. The WHO, in collaboration with UNFPA and UNICEF, published Investing in Our Future: A Framework for Accelerated Action for the Sexual and Reproductive Health of Young People in 2006. 18. The United Nations Committee on the Rights of the Child issued General Comment No. 4 during its 33rd session, addressing adolescent health and development in the context of the Convention on the Rights of the Child. 19. The WHO published guidelines on making health services adolescent-friendly, emphasizing the development of national quality standards for adolescent health services. 20. Hodgkin R and Newell P authored the third edition of the Implementation Handbook for the Convention on the Rights of the Child, providing practical guidance for implementing the Convention. 21. The United Nations adopted the Convention on the Rights of the Child (CRC) in 1989, emphasizing the protection and promotion of children's rights globally. 22. The WHO published a policy brief in 2012 on integrating sexual and reproductive health into health emergency and disaster risk management. 23. The WHO's Implementing Best Practices Initiative focuses on family planning for health and development, providing actionable recommendations for change. 24. Senlet P, Cagatay L, Ergin J, and Mathis J explored the integration of family planning with abortion services in Turkey, as published in the International Family Planning Perspectives. 25. The International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights (ICCPR), adopted in 1966, outlines the civil and political rights of individuals and the obligations of states to uphold them. 26. The European Court of Human Rights addressed cases such as Pichon and Sajous v. France (2001) and RR v. Poland (2011), emphasizing the protection of human rights in healthcare contexts. 27. Bradley SEK, Schwandt HM, and Khan S analyzed levels, trends, and reasons for contraceptive discontinuation in their DHS Analytical Studies No. 20, published in 2009. 28. Jain AK, Rama Rao S, Kim J, and Costello M evaluated an intervention to improve the quality of care in family planning programs in the Philippines, as published in the Journal of Biosocial Science in 2012. 29. Darroch JE and Singh S analyzed trends in contraceptive need and use in developing countries between 2003 and 2012, as published in The Lancet in 2013. 30. Bruce J outlined the fundamental elements of quality care in family planning, presenting a simple framework in Studies in Family Planning in 1990. 31. The WHO published Sexual and Reproductive Health: Core Competencies in Primary Care in 2011, providing a framework for healthcare providers. 32. Faden RR and Beauchamp TL authored A History and Theory of Informed Consent, published by Oxford University Press in 1986. 33. The WHO published Family Planning: A Global Handbook for Providers in 2011, offering updated guidance for family planning services. 34. Desjardins M discussed the politics of sterilization of individuals with intellectual disabilities in the book Sex and Disability, edited by McRuer R and Mollow A, published by Duke University Press in 2012. 35. The International Federation of Gynecology and Obstetrics published guidelines on ethical issues in managing severely disabled women with gynecological problems in 2011. 36. The Council of Europe adopted the Convention on Human Rights and Biomedicine in Oviedo in 1997, addressing the application of biology and medicine in human rights. 37. The United Nations Development Programme published Investing in Development: A Practical Plan to Achieve the Millennium Development Goals in 2005. 38. The United Nations Secretary-General launched the Global Strategy for Women’s and Children’s Health, emphasizing the importance of participation and human rights in improving health outcomes. 39. Potts H explored the relationship between participation and the right to the highest attainable standard of health in a publication by the University of Essex Human Rights Centre in 2008. 40. The United Nations Committee on the Elimination of Discrimination Against Women issued General Recommendation No. 23 during its 16th session, focusing on political and public life. 41. The Office of the United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights published technical guidance on applying a human rights-based approach to reducing preventable maternal morbidity and mortality. 42. The Commission on Information and Accountability for Women’s and Children’s Health published its first progress report on implementing recommendations in 2012. 43. The WHO published Keeping Promises, Measuring Results, a report on accountability for women’s and children’s health, in 2011. 44. The United Nations General Assembly adopted the Basic Principles and Guidelines on the Right to a Remedy and Reparation for Victims of Gross Violations of International Human Rights Law in 2005. 45. The Human Rights Committee issued General Comment No. 31 during its 80th session, addressing the general legal obligations of states under the ICCPR. 46. The International Law Commission provided commentary on Article 34 of the Draft Articles on Responsibility of States for Internationally Wrongful Acts in 2001. 47. Bueno de Mesquita J and Hunt P emphasized the human rights responsibility of donors in providing international assistance and cooperation in sexual and reproductive health in a publication by the University of Essex Human Rights Centre in 2008.
